Nina (AE): Heads-up — Finly (large fintech) opened ticket #36812 asking for streamed function/tool calls that emit partial structured frames so their UI can render progressive results and their backend can act on intermediate tool outputs. They called this 'progressive toolchain'.
Rahul (support): Yep, ticket attached. Current behavior: model emits a single fn_call at the end; customer wants multiple toolcall events as they are discovered. They need schema stability (v1) and an audit trail for each tool event.
Casey (product): Important to scope: are they asking that frames be valid JSON objects per-frame, plus a final merged JSON? Any auth/attestation asks?
Nina (AE): Exactly. Example they sent:
```
{
  "frame":1, "event":"toolcall", "tool":"kyc_lookup", "args":{"ssn":"***"}
}
{
  "frame":2, "event":"toolcall", "tool":"risk_score", "args":{"account_id":987}
}
{
  "final", "event":"result", "payload":{"customer_id":987, "kyc":"pass", "risk":42}
}
```
They also asked for optional HMAC signing of final object and per-frame timestamps in logs.
Olivia (eng): Implementation notes: runtime currently streams tokens. We can introduce an event envelope that is emitted mid-stream. Main challenges: (1) function boundary semantics — we need to allow nested/interleaved calls, (2) batching/throughput effects when many tiny frames are emitted, (3) SDK ergonomics for rehydration into a single object.
Jun (infra): Observability needs: per-frame tracing id, ability to filter toolcall frames in logs, and retention of audit logs for pilot. Dedicated customers can opt-in to longer retention.
Casey (product): Propose three tiers for planning/prioritization:
- Tier A (fast pilot): Add opaque event framing for toolcall frames, no server-side schema validation, SDK returns raw frames. Minimal changes to runtime.
- Tier B (recommended): Framing + server-side schema validation and versioning, SDK helpers to stitch frames, and advisory docs for migration.
- Tier C (full): All of B + canary rollout hooks, Dedicated routing guarantees, HMAC signing option, and observability + billing metrics per frame.
Rahul (support): Finly prefers Tier B. They explicitly asked for schema validation and a pinned schema version so their pipeline doesn't break.
Casey (product): Cost/impact: more frames = more RPCs and could lower batching efficiency. Need an estimate of latency and cost delta. Also need to preserve backward compatibility for clients expecting final fn_call only.
Olivia (eng): Rough estimate: prototype (framing + simple SDK) 2 weeks; full Tier B ~8 weeks with 1 FE (SDK) + 2 BE (runtime/gateway/obs). Risk: batching interactions could increase GPU cost by ~5-15% depending on workload.
Nina (AE): Finly said they'd pilot in Dedicated if we can promise dedicated pool and a targeted latency SLA: per-frame tail <250ms.
Casey (product): Acceptance criteria for a pilot (Tier B):
1) Event envelope documented and backward-compatible parsing rules.
2) Server-side optional schema validation with versioning API.
3) SDK helper that emits a rehydrated final JSON plus raw frame stream.
4) Observability: per-frame traces and audit log export.
5) Latency/regression tests showing <10% degradation vs baseline on pilot workload.
Jun (infra): We'll need a canary plan and a fallback where clients can request "final-only" mode until they adopt frames. Also add rate-limiting knobs to avoid DOS from noisy frames.
Casey (product): Next steps: Nina to confirm SLA + Dedicated commitment from Finly. Rahul attach ticket and sample logs. Olivia to produce RFC w/ rough milestones by next Tue. I'll add this as customer-driven candidate and propose Tier B as Q3 stretch if Eng resourcing aligns.
Nina (AE): I'll get SLA confirmation today.
Rahul (support): Ticket: https://redwood.corp/tickets/36812 (internal). Attached sample transcripts.
Olivia (eng): Will start RFC draft Monday.
Casey (product): Quick sync Friday 9am PT to finalize backlog placement.
